html:
These views draw the modules the way software draws modules and their interfaces. Each rectangle is a whole module (the SBGN submap glyph, which stands for a pathway drawn elsewhere), and each molecule between two rectangles is an interface: a molecule one module declares as its output and another declares as its input. The arrow runs from the module that makes the molecule; the plain line runs into the module that takes it. One molecule taken by two modules is drawn once, with a line to each.

Only declared interfaces are drawn. Several modules take hydrogen peroxide or the NOX2 holoenzyme as an input that no module yet declares as an output, so those inputs have no rectangle on their left here. The views are built from the modules' declarations (tools/module_view.py), so they change when a module's inputs or outputs change.

The draft with open sockets adds, as a white molecule on a dashed line, each input a module expects from another module of the set that no module provides yet. Inputs from the exposure (the particle, endotoxin, CpG-DNA), cofactors and building blocks (NADPH, oxygen, amino acids, heme) and a module's own proteins are not sockets and are left out.
